sentences.text: 3. During pendency of the petition, both the parties i.e., petitioner-accused No.1 and respondent No.2 filed Joint Divorce petition under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1956 and got divorce in M.C.No.17/2023 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Gubbi and both the parties have filed I.A.Nos.1/2023 under Section 320(2) read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. along with the joint affidavit in both the cases seeking permission of this Court to compound the offences.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the respondents.

5. Though the Police have filed the charge-sheet against the accused Nos.1 to 3 for the for the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC, the injury Nos.1 to 3 are simple in nature, all injuries are contusions and there is no weapon used by the accused to attempt to commit murder and it is family dispute between the husband and wife and subsequently, turned into criminal case.
6.
Considering the same, I am of the view, the offence under Section 307 of IPC shall not be attracted.
There is no hurdle for this Court for allowing the parties to compound the offence.

7. In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in 2012 CRI.L.J.4934 wherein, it has been held that in cases where the parties have settled the dispute between them in respect of a matrimonial case, the Court can quash the proceedings.
- -6- 8.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I.A.Nos.1/2023 in both the cases are allowed.
The parties are permitted to compound the offence.
Consequently, both the petitions are allowed.

The criminal proceedings against the petitioners in S.C.No.1571/2021 on the file of XIV Additional City Civil and Session Judge, Bengaluru in Crl.P.No.7799/2020 and C.C.No.7702/2022 pending on the file of Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC, Tiptur, Tumakuru in Crl.P.No.6512/2022 are hereby quashed.
